args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks following the deploy of v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west); service status showed healthy=false with an 18% error rate. Deployment history confirmed v2.3.1 as unhealthy and v2.3.0 as the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy). Action taken: rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions; rollback reported status rolled_out and verified across us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Follow-up needed: confirm error rate recovers on v2.3.0 and investigate root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before any redeploy.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

**Investigation**
- checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west, reporting unhealthy with an 18% error rate.
- Release history showed v2.3.1 as unhealthy; v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc was excluded — it was staging-only and also unhealthy.)

**Rollback**
- Rolled checkout-api back to **v2.3.0** in all three production regions. The rollback reported `rolled_out` and was verified.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. The summary covers the symptoms, the rollback performed, and recommended follow-ups (confirm error rate recovery on v2.3.0 and root-cause the v2.3.1 regression before any redeploy).

One thing worth doing next: re-check `get_service_status` in a few minutes to confirm the error rate has actually dropped on v2.3.0 — I did not verify post-rollback health beyond the rollout confirmation.
